title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Methods, Optogenetics experiments with 3D joint kinematics; Fig. 2h-j; Extended Data Fig. 3; Genotypes table (page 29)
quote: DNg100 activation produced forward walking on the ball, but at a lower speed than is typical of wild-type flies [53].
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 (also notes it is BDN2); the line VT058557-AD x R85F12-DBD is listed in driver_lines.csv as BDN2-splitGal4 -> DNg100.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front left body-coxa joint; 5 s on; 0.03, 0.09 and 0.33 mW/mm2 (strongest 0.33 mW/mm2)
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill
frequency_note: L1 step frequency read from Fig. 2j: medians about 3.5, 5 and 5.5 Hz at 0.03, 0.09, 0.33 mW/mm2; increased with intensity
coordination_notes: generally tetrapod coordination (Extended Data Fig. 3); all six legs tracked
n_flies_note: n=7 flies, 8 trials per fly per intensity
notes: Velocity and step frequency increased with laser intensity; outcome the same (walking) at all intensities, so one record. Line specificity not stated in paper (confocal VNC image only). Expression from split-GAL4 is bilateral; light was focused on the front left leg region. Simulation scores for DNg100 seen in Fig. 1e/text, not used as evidence.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Results, 'A separate class of descending neurons recruits an overlapping rhythm generating circuit'; Fig. 5c-e; Genotypes table (page 29)
quote: we optogenetically activated DNb08 neurons in decapitated flies and found that they reliably produced rhythmic leg movements (Fig. 5c–e, Supplementary Video 2).
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNb08; SS70620 maps to DNb08 alone in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front left body-coxa joint; 5 s on; intensity not stated
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered; movements evoked more reliably with the spherical treadmill removed (legs unloaded)
coordination_notes: front and middle left femur-tibia joints oscillate; resembled searching movements rather than coordinated walking
n_flies_note: n=10 flies, 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly
notes: Fig. 5e: kinematic rhythmicity score higher stim on vs off for left front (p=0.036) and left middle (p=0.004) legs; hind legs not reported. Text: movements 'resembled the searching movements that insects exhibit when their legs are not in contact with the ground' and were 'evoked more reliably when the spherical treadmill was removed'. Headless surface coded air (cartoon in Fig. 5d shows no ball); some trials were apparently on the treadmill. Specificity not stated in paper; kit lists SS70620 as DNb08 only and the Fig. 5c VNC image shows only DN axons. Simulation scores for DNb08 seen (Fig. 1e, Fig. 5a,b), not used as evidence.
